[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Healthcare applications require scheduled batch processing for nightly claims adjudication, financial reconciliation, reporting generation, and ETL pipelines. Long-running jobs need resource isolation, parallel execution, failure recovery, and monitoring.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Implement batch processing pattern using Kubernetes Jobs for one-time tasks and CronJobs for scheduled execution. Leverage Job parallelism for distributed processing, pod resource quotas preventing resource exhaustion, automatic restart on failure, and completion tracking with alerting.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- Scheduled nightly/monthly batch processes (claims adjudication, reporting)
- ETL pipelines loading data warehouses
- Data migration and transformation jobs
- Model training and batch inference for ML
page_texts.7:
[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- **Scheduled Execution**: CronJobs for reliable recurring batch jobs
- **Parallelism**: Process millions of records via distributed pods
- **Resource Isolation**: Batch jobs don't impact real-time services
- **Automatic Retry**: Failed jobs restart automatically
- **Completion Tracking**: Job status monitoring and alerting

## Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **Platform Engineer**: Configures Kubernetes CronJob and Job resources, resource quotas, and monitoring for batch workloads.

- **DevOps Engineer**: Builds and maintains CI/CD pipelines for batch job container images and deployment automation.
- **Application Architect**: Determines when to use batch processing and designs job partitioning and retry strategies.

[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

**Batch Processing on Kubernetes:**

- **CronJob**: Scheduled batch execution (cron syntax)
- **Job**: One-time or parallel batch tasks
- **Parallelism**: Distribute work across multiple pods
- **Completions**: Track successful task completion
- **Backoff Limit**: Automatic retry with exponential backoff
- **TTL**: Auto-cleanup completed jobs

[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```text
Batch Processing Architecture
==============================

[ CronJob: Schedule ]
       ↓ creates
[ Job: Batch Workload ]
       ↓ spawns
[ Parallel Pods: completions=100, parallelism=10 ]
       ↓ reads
[ S3 / Database: Input Data ]
       ↓ processes
[ Business Logic ]
       ↓ writes
[ S3 / Database: Output Data ]
       ↓ tracks
[ Job Completion: Success/Failure ]
       ↓ retries (on failure)
[ Failed Pods: Automatic Retry ]

Features:

- Parallel Processing: 10 concurrent pods
- Fault Tolerance: Pod restart on failure
- Resource Management: Spot instances
```

[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#configuration-example]

### Configuration Example

```yaml
# CronJob: Nightly Claims Adjudication
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: nightly-claims-adjudication
  namespace: production
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *" # 2 AM daily
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid # Don't start if previous job still running
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      parallelism: 20 # 20 parallel pods
      completions: 100 # Process 100 batches total
      backoffLimit: 3 # Retry up to 3 times
      ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400 # Cleanup after 24 hours
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app: claims-adjudication
            job-type: batch
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          serviceAccountName: claims-batch-sa

          # Pod-level security context (recommended: GUID-SEC-APPS-KUBERNETES-PLATFORM-2.7.04)
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 10000
            fsGroup: 10000
            seccompProfile:
              type: RuntimeDefault

          containers:
          - name: adjudication
            image: 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/claims-batch:v2.1.0

            # Container-level security context (recommended: Pod Security Standards - Restricted)
            securityContext:
              allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
              runAsNonRoot: true
              runAsUser: 10000
              capabilities:
                drop: ["ALL"]
              readOnlyRootFilesystem: true

            # Writable directories (required for readOnlyRootFilesystem)
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
            - name: work
              mountPath: /work

            resources:
              requests:
                memory: "2Gi"
                cpu: "1000m"
              limits:
                memory: "4Gi"
                cpu: "2000m"

            env:
            - name: BATCH_SIZE
              value: "10000"
            - name: PROCESSING_DATE
              value: "$(date +%Y-%m-%d)"

            # Secret from External Secrets Operator (recommended: PTN-SEC-SECRETS-001)
            - name: DATABASE_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: batch-secrets-external  # Created by ExternalSecret CRD
                  key: database.password

          volumes:
          - name: tmp
            emptyDir: {}
          - name: work
            emptyDir: {}
```

[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#phase-1-deploy-simple-batch-job]

#### Phase 1: Deploy Simple Batch Job

1. **Create one-time Job** for data migration:

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: claims-migration
  namespace: batch-jobs
spec:
  # Job will complete when 1 pod succeeds
  completions: 1

  # No parallelism (single pod runs)
  parallelism: 1

  # Retry up to 3 times on failure
  backoffLimit: 3

  # Job times out after 2 hours
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 7200

  # Cleanup completed job after 24 hours
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400

  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: claims-migration
        job-type: batch
    spec:
      restartPolicy: OnFailure

      # Pod-level security context (recommended: GUID-SEC-APPS-KUBERNETES-PLATFORM-2.7.04)
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10000
        fsGroup: 10000
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault

      containers:
      - name: migration
        image: 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/claims-migration:v1.0

        # Container-level security context (recommended: Pod Security Standards - Restricted)
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10000
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true

        # Writable directories for batch processing
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tmp
          mountPath: /tmp
        - name: work
          mountPath: /work

        # Resource requests for batch pod
        resources:
          requests:
            memory: "2Gi"
            cpu: "1000m"
          limits:
            memory: "4Gi"
            cpu: "2000m"

        env:
        - name: SOURCE_DATABASE
          value: "postgres://old-db:5432/claims"
        - name: TARGET_DATABASE
          value: "postgres://new-db:5432/claims"
        - name: BATCH_SIZE
          value: "10000"

        # Secret from External Secrets Operator (recommended: PTN-SEC-SECRETS-001)
        - name: DATABASE_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: migration-secrets-external  # Created by ExternalSecret CRD
              key: database.password

      volumes:
      - name: tmp
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: work
        emptyDir: {}
```

1. **Run Job and monitor progress**:

```bash
kubectl apply -f claims-migration-job.yaml

# Watch Job status
kubectl get jobs -n batch-jobs -w

# View pod logs
kubectl logs -n batch-jobs -l app=claims-migration --follow

# Check Job completion
kubectl describe job claims-migration -n batch-jobs
```

1. **Verify Job completion**:

```bash
# Job status should show "1/1 Completions"
kubectl get job claims-migration -n batch-jobs
# NAME                COMPLETIONS   DURATION   AGE
# claims-migration    1/1           15m        16m
```

[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#phase-2-implement-parallel-batch-processing]

#### Phase 2: Implement Parallel Batch Processing

1. **Create Job with work queue parallelism**:

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: nightly-adjudication
  namespace: batch-jobs
spec:
  # Process 100 batches total
  completions: 100

  # Run 20 pods in parallel
  parallelism: 20

  # Each pod processes 1 batch, completes, and exits
  completionMode: Indexed  # Pods get index 0-99

  backoffLimit: 5
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 28800  # 8 hour timeout
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400

  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: OnFailure

      # Avoid running batch jobs on nodes with real-time services
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - weight: 100
            podAffinityTerm:
              labelSelector:
                matchExpressions:
                - key: workload-type
                  operator: In
                  values:
                  - realtime
              topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname

      # Pod-level security context
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10000
        fsGroup: 10000
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault

      containers:
      - name: adjudication
        image: 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/claims-adjudication:v2.1.0

        # Container-level security context
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10000
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true

        volumeMounts:
        - name: tmp
          mountPath: /tmp
        - name: work
          mountPath: /work

        resources:
          requests:
            memory: "2Gi"
            cpu: "1000m"
          limits:
            memory: "4Gi"
            cpu: "2000m"

        env:
        # JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX is set by Kubernetes (0-99)
        - name: BATCH_INDEX
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.annotations['batch.kubernetes.io/job-completion-index']
        - name: TOTAL_BATCHES
          value: "100"
        - name: PROCESSING_DATE
          value: "2026-02-03"
        - name: S3_BUCKET
          value: "gainwell-claims-data"

        # Command processes specific batch based on index
        command:
        - /app/process_batch.sh
        - --batch-index=$(BATCH_INDEX)
        - --total-batches=$(TOTAL_BATCHES)
        - --date=$(PROCESSING_DATE)
```

1. **Monitor parallel Job execution**:

```bash
# Watch pods spinning up in parallel
kubectl get pods -n batch-jobs -l job-name=nightly-adjudication -w

# Check Job progress
kubectl get job nightly-adjudication -n batch-jobs
# NAME                    COMPLETIONS   DURATION
# nightly-adjudication    45/100        25m

# View logs from specific batch
kubectl logs -n batch-jobs nightly-adjudication-15  # Pod processing batch 15
```

1. **Create work queue processing pattern** (for dynamic work distribution):

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: claims-queue-processor
spec:
  parallelism: 10  # 10 workers
  completions: 10  # Each worker processes until queue empty

  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
      containers:
      - name: processor
        image: queue-processor:v1.0
        env:
        - name: QUEUE_URL
          value: "https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/123456789012/claims-queue"

        # Worker pulls messages from SQS until queue empty
        command:
        - python
        - process_queue.py
        - --queue-url=$(QUEUE_URL)
        - --batch-size=100
```

[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#phase-3-configure-cronjob-for-scheduled-execution]

#### Phase 3: Configure CronJob for Scheduled Execution

1. **Create CronJob for nightly processing**:

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: nightly-claims-adjudication
  namespace: batch-jobs
spec:
  # Run at 2:00 AM daily (cron syntax)
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"

  # Prevent multiple instances running simultaneously
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid

  # Start Job within 5 minutes of scheduled time, or skip
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 300

  # Keep last 3 successful Jobs for history
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3

  # Keep last 1 failed Job for debugging
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1

  # Suspend CronJob (useful for maintenance)
  suspend: false

  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      parallelism: 20
      completions: 100
      backoffLimit: 3
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 28800  # 8 hours
      ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400

      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app: claims-adjudication
            job-type: batch
            schedule: nightly
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          serviceAccountName: claims-batch-sa

          # Priority for batch jobs (lower than real-time)
          priorityClassName: batch-priority

          containers:
          - name: adjudication
            image: 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/claims-adjudication:v2.1.0
            resources:
              requests:
                memory: "2Gi"
                cpu: "1000m"
              limits:
                memory: "4Gi"
                cpu: "2000m"

            env:
            - name: BATCH_INDEX
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: metadata.annotations['batch.kubernetes.io/job-completion-index']
            - name: PROCESSING_DATE
              value: "$(date -d yesterday +%Y-%m-%d)"  # Process previous day
            - name: S3_INPUT_BUCKET
              value: "gainwell-claims-raw"
            - name: S3_OUTPUT_BUCKET
              value: "gainwell-claims-adjudicated"

            # Liveness probe to detect hung processing
            livenessProbe:
              exec:
                command:
                - /app/health_check.sh
              initialDelaySeconds: 300
              periodSeconds: 60
              timeoutSeconds: 10
              failureThreshold: 3
```

1. **Create multiple CronJobs for different schedules**:

```yaml
---
# Hourly reporting
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: hourly-metrics-aggregation
  namespace: batch-jobs
spec:
  schedule: "0 * * * *"  # Every hour
  concurrencyPolicy: Replace  # Kill old job if still running
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: aggregator
            image: metrics-aggregator:v1.0

---
# Weekly data archival
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: weekly-data-archive
  namespace: batch-jobs
spec:
  schedule: "0 3 * * 0"  # 3 AM every Sunday
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: archiver
            image: data-archiver:v1.0

---
# Monthly financial close
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: monthly-financial-close
  namespace: batch-jobs
spec:
  schedule: "0 1 1 * *"  # 1 AM on 1st of each month
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 43200  # 12 hour timeout for month-end processing
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: close
            image: financial-close:v1.0
```

1. **Manually trigger CronJob** (for testing or ad-hoc runs):

```bash
kubectl create job --from=cronjob/nightly-claims-adjudication \
  manual-run-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S) \

  -n batch-jobs
```

[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#phase-4-implement-failure-handling-and-retry-logic]

#### Phase 4: Implement Failure Handling and Retry Logic

1. **Configure exponential backoff retry**:

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: resilient-batch-job
spec:
  # Retry up to 5 times
  backoffLimit: 5

  # Kubernetes implements exponential backoff automatically
  # Retry delays: 10s, 20s, 40s, 80s, 160s

  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: OnFailure  # Required for backoffLimit to work

      containers:
      - name: processor
        image: batch-processor:v1.0

        # Application implements idempotent processing
        # Can safely retry on failure without duplicates
        command:
        - python
        - process.py
        - --idempotent
        - --checkpoint-file=/mnt/checkpoint/state.json

        volumeMounts:
        - name: checkpoint
          mountPath: /mnt/checkpoint

      volumes:
      - name: checkpoint
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: batch-checkpoint-pvc
```

1. **Implement dead letter queue for failed items**:

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: batch-with-dlq
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: processor
        image: batch-processor:v1.0
        env:
        - name: DLQ_URL
          value: "https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/123456789012/claims-dlq"

        # Application code:
        # try:
        #   process_claim(claim)
        # except Exception as e:
        #   send_to_dlq(claim, error=str(e))
        #   logger.error(f"Failed claim {claim.id}: {e}")
        #   # Don't raise - continue processing other claims
```

1. **Monitor Job failures and alert**:

```yaml
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: batch-job-alerts
  namespace: batch-jobs
spec:
  groups:

  - name: batch_jobs
    interval: 60s
    rules:
    - alert: BatchJobFailed
      expr: kube_job_status_failed{namespace="batch-jobs"} > 0
      for: 5m
      labels:
        severity: critical
      annotations:
        summary: "Batch Job {{ $labels.job_name }} failed"
        description: "Job has failed and requires investigation"

    - alert: BatchJobRunningTooLong
      expr: time() - kube_job_status_start_time{namespace="batch-jobs"} > 14400
      for: 5m
      labels:
        severity: warning
      annotations:
        summary: "Job {{ $labels.job_name }} running >4 hours"
        description: "Job may be stuck or processing slowly"

    - alert: CronJobNotScheduled
      expr: time() - kube_cronjob_status_last_schedule_time > 7200
      for: 10m
      labels:
        severity: warning
      annotations:
        summary: "CronJob {{ $labels.cronjob }} not scheduled in 2 hours"
        description: "CronJob may be suspended or misconfigured"
```

[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#phase-5-optimize-resource-usage-and-cost]

#### Phase 5: Optimize Resource Usage and Cost

1. **Use PriorityClass for batch workloads**:

```yaml
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: batch-priority
value: 100  # Lower than default (1000)
globalDefault: false
description: "Low priority for batch jobs, can be preempted by real-time workloads"
preemptionPolicy: PreemptLowerPriority

---
# Real-time workload priority
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: realtime-priority
value: 10000
globalDefault: false
description: "High priority for real-time services"
```

1. **Configure batch Jobs to use Spot instances**:

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: cost-optimized-batch
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      priorityClassName: batch-priority

      # Tolerate Spot instance interruption
      tolerations:
      - key: "eks.amazonaws.com/capacityType"
        operator: "Equal"
        value: "SPOT"
        effect: "NoSchedule"

      # Node affinity for Spot instances
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - weight: 100
            preference:
              matchExpressions:
              - key: eks.amazonaws.com/capacityType
                operator: In
                values:
                - SPOT

      containers:
      - name: processor
        image: batch-processor:v1.0

        # Implement checkpointing for resumability
        command:
        - python
        - process.py
        - --checkpoint-interval=300  # Save state every 5 minutes
        - --checkpoint-s3=s3://gainwell-batch-checkpoints/
```

1. **Use EKS Auto-mode NodePool for batch node provisioning**:

```yaml
apiVersion: eks.amazonaws.com/v1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: batch-nodepool
spec:
  capacityType: spot  # Spot only for batch workloads
  instanceTypes:
    - c5.2xlarge
    - c5.4xlarge
    - m5.2xlarge
  scaling:
    minSize: 0  # Scale to zero when no batch jobs
    maxSize: 100
  # Labels for batch nodes
  labels:
    workload-type: batch

  # Taints to prevent non-batch workloads
  taints:
    - key: batch-only
      value: "true"
      effect: NoSchedule
```

[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- **Idempotent Processing**: Design batch logic to be idempotent (safe to retry). Use unique transaction IDs and check for already-processed records.
- **Parallelism Strategy**: Use indexed completions for fixed-size batches. Use work queue pattern for dynamic workloads.
- **Resource Requests**: Set accurate CPU/memory requests to prevent starvation. Batch jobs should not starve real-time services.
- **Concurrency Control**: Use `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` for CronJobs to prevent overlapping runs that could cause data corruption.
- **Timeout Configuration**: Set `activeDeadlineSeconds` to kill hung jobs. Prevents zombie jobs consuming resources indefinitely.
- **Checkpointing**: Implement checkpointing for long-running jobs (>2 hours). Enables resumption after Spot interruption or failure.
- **Dead Letter Queue**: Send failed items to DLQ for later reprocessing. Don't fail entire job due to single bad record.
- **Monitoring**: Alert on job failures, long runtimes, and CronJob scheduling issues. Track job duration trends.
- **Cost Optimization**: Use Spot instances for batch workloads (50-90% cost savings). Implement graceful shutdown on SIGTERM.
- **Separation of Concerns**: Use dedicated namespace and node pools for batch jobs to prevent resource contention with real-time services.
- **Security Hardening**: Follow Pod Security Standards (Restricted) for batch jobs with same rigor as real-time services.

[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#security-configuration-explained]

### Security Configuration Explained

Batch jobs follow the same security recommendations as real-time workloads:

**Pod Security Standards (Restricted):**

- `runAsNonRoot: true` - Batch jobs must not run as root despite offline processing nature
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` - Immutable container filesystem; use emptyDir volumes for work directories
- `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` - Prevents privilege escalation even in batch context
- `capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]` - Removes all Linux capabilities minimizing attack surface
- `seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault` - Applies syscall filtering to batch workloads

**Rationale**: Batch jobs often process sensitive data (PHI claims, financial records) and run with elevated AWS IAM permissions (S3 access). Compromised batch pods could exfiltrate large datasets. Security controls recommended by GUID-SEC-APPS-KUBERNETES-PLATFORM-2.7.04 --> --> §2.1 apply equally to batch workloads.

**External Secrets Management:**
Batch jobs reference secrets created by External Secrets Operator ([PTN-SEC-K8S-003](../../security/kubernetes/PTN-SEC-K8S-003-security-secrets-management-pattern.md)) rather than native Kubernetes Secrets. Benefits for batch workloads:

- Database credentials rotated without CronJob reconfiguration
- CloudTrail audit trail of secret access during batch execution
- Centralized secrets management across batch and real-time services
- HIPAA compliance for encryption at rest (§164.312(a)(2)(iv))

**Container Image Security:**
Batch job container images must follow GUID-SEC-APPS-CONTAINER-SECURITY-2.7.05 --> -->:

- Distroless or minimal base images reducing attack surface
- Multi-stage builds excluding development tools from production batch images
- Image signing with Cosign for supply chain integrity
- SBOM generation enabling vulnerability tracking for batch processing dependencies
- Non-root user in Dockerfile compatible with `runAsUser: 10000`

[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Missing restartPolicy: OnFailure**: Without this, failed pods don't retry and job backoffLimit doesn't work.
    - **Solution**: Always set `restartPolicy: OnFailure` in Job template spec.

- **Overlapping CronJob Runs**: Previous run still processing when new run starts, causing data corruption.
    - **Solution**: Use `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` to prevent overlaps. Monitor job duration to ensure completion within schedule interval.

- **Resource Exhaustion**: Batch job with high parallelism starves real-time pods.
    - **Solution**: Use ResourceQuotas for batch namespace. Set appropriate parallelism (don't exceed cluster capacity).

- **Zombie Jobs**: Failed jobs not cleaned up, accumulating and consuming resources.
    - **Solution**: Set `ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400` (24 hours). Monitor and delete old failed jobs.

- **Non-Idempotent Processing**: Retry on failure causes duplicate processing (e.g., double-billing).
    - **Solution**: Use unique transaction IDs. Check if record already processed before processing.

- **Large Job Manifest ConfigMaps**: Embedding large datasets in Job env vars hits size limits.
    - **Solution**: Store data in S3/database. Pass only S3 paths or query parameters to Job.

- **Spot Instance Interruptions**: Spot termination kills batch job mid-processing without checkpoint.
    - **Solution**: Implement SIGTERM handler to save checkpoint. Use backoffLimit for automatic retry.

[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#configuration-example]

### Configuration Example

```yaml
# Complete Batch Processing Example
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: nightly-claims-adjudication
  namespace: batch-jobs
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      parallelism: 20
      completions: 100
      completionMode: Indexed
      backoffLimit: 3
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 28800
      ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400

      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app: claims-adjudication
            job-type: batch
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          priorityClassName: batch-priority
          serviceAccountName: claims-batch-sa

          tolerations:
          - key: batch-only
            operator: Equal
            value: "true"
            effect: NoSchedule

          containers:
          - name: adjudication
            image: 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/claims-adjudication:v2.1.0
            resources:
              requests:
                memory: "2Gi"
                cpu: "1000m"
              limits:
                memory: "4Gi"
                cpu: "2000m"

            env:
            - name: BATCH_INDEX
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: metadata.annotations['batch.kubernetes.io/job-completion-index']
            - name: TOTAL_BATCHES
              value: "100"
            - name: PROCESSING_DATE
              value: "$(date -d yesterday +%Y-%m-%d)"
```

### Compliance Requirements

**Security Controls (Recommended):**

- Pod Security Standards (Restricted) enforcement for batch Jobs/CronJobs
- External secrets management (AWS Secrets Manager via External Secrets Operator)
- Container images signed with Cosign and verified at deployment
- SBOM generation for batch processing container images
- Non-root containers with read-only root filesystem
- Resource limits preventing denial-of-service and resource exhaustion
- Service accounts with least-privilege IAM roles (IRSA) for S3/database access

**Batch Processing Standards:**

- Audit Logging: Batch job execution logs retained for 90 days (HIPAA compliance)
- Data Processing Records: Track which claims/transactions processed in each batch run
- Failure Notifications: Critical batch job failures trigger immediate alerts to on-call
- Processing Windows: Nightly batch jobs must complete before 8 AM business hours

**HIPAA Requirements (for PHI batch processing):**

- Encryption at rest: KMS-encrypted EBS volumes for checkpoint data, encrypted S3 buckets
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+ for database connections, S3 API calls
- Audit logging: Comprehensive logs of PHI data access during batch processing
- Access controls: Least-privilege service accounts, RBAC restricting Job creation
- See [PTN-SEC-K8S-001](../../security/kubernetes/PTN-SEC-K8S-001-security-hipaa-compliance-pattern.md) for complete batch workload requirements

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| **Job Success Rate** | >99% | Prometheus: `kube_job_status_succeeded / kube_job_status_completion_time` |
| **Job Duration** | Within processing window | Prometheus: `kube_job_status_completion_time - kube_job_status_start_time` |

| **CronJob Schedule Adherence** | >98% on-time | `kube_cronjob_status_last_schedule_time` vs. scheduled time |
| **Batch Processing Cost** | Within budget | Kubecost: batch namespace cost per processing window |

### Real-World Example 1: Nightly Claims Adjudication

**Context**: Claims adjudication runs nightly in an 8-hour window (2 AM - 10 AM)

**Implementation**:

- CronJob scheduled at 2:00 AM with 100 completions, 20 parallelism (20 pods)
- Each pod processes 12,000 claims (1.2M / 100 batches)
- Spot instances with checkpointing every 10 minutes (resume on interruption)
- Dead letter queue for failed claims (manual review next day)
- Prometheus alert if job duration >7 hours (warning) or job fails (critical)

**Outcome**: High job success rate; failures retried automatically

### Real-World Example 2: Monthly Financial Reconciliation

**Context**: Complex month-end close requiring 12-hour processing window

**Implementation**:

- CronJob on 1st of month at 1:00 AM
- Single-pod Job (no parallelism due to complex cross-account reconciliation)
- 16 CPU, 64GB memory for large dataset processing
- On-Demand instances (criticality requires reliability)
- Slack notification on completion with summary report
- Manual approval workflow before finalizing close

**Outcome**: 100% on-time completion; automated the majority of manual effort

### Real-World Example 3: ETL Pipeline for Data Warehouse

**Context**: Hourly ETL loading data from operational databases to Redshift

**Implementation**:

- CronJob every hour (schedule: "0 ** **")
- Work queue pattern: Job pulls tasks from SQS queue
- 10 parallel workers processing different tables simultaneously
- Idempotent inserts (upsert on conflict)
- Karpenter scales nodes based on queue depth
- Cost-optimized: nodes scale to zero during low-traffic hours (2 AM - 6 AM)

**Outcome**: Low average latency (data available in warehouse within 1 hour)

#### Before (Manual/VM-Based Batch Processing)

- **Scheduling**: Cron on EC2 instances; manual start for ad-hoc runs
- **Failure Handling**: Manual restart required; no automatic retry
- **Parallelism**: Single-threaded processing; long runtime
- **Resource Utilization**: Always-on EC2 instances (24/7 cost)
- **Monitoring**: CloudWatch logs; manual checking for failures
- **Cost**: Always-on EC2 instances with no idle scale-down
page_texts.43:
[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#after-kubernetes-batch-pattern]

#### After (Kubernetes Batch Pattern)

- **Scheduling**: Declarative CronJobs; easy ad-hoc triggers
- **Failure Handling**: Automatic retry with backoffLimit; DLQ for failures
- **Parallelism**: 20-way parallelism; significantly reduced runtime
- **Resource Utilization**: Auto-scaling Spot nodes; scale to zero when idle
- **Monitoring**: Prometheus alerts; PagerDuty integration for failures
- **Cost**: Reduced cost with Spot instances and auto-scaling

[patterns/application/kubernetes/PTN-APP-K8S-001-application-batch-processing-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Healthcare batch processing (nightly claims, reporting, ETL) requires scheduled execution, parallelism, failure recovery, and resource isolation within time windows.

**Solution:** Kubernetes CronJobs for scheduling, Job parallelism for distributed processing, backoffLimit for automatic retry, PriorityClass for resource isolation, Spot instances for cost optimization.

**When to Use:** Scheduled batch processes (nightly/monthly), ETL pipelines, data migrations, ML model training, report generation.

**Key Benefits:**

- Scheduled execution via CronJobs
- Distributed parallelism (20x faster processing)
- Automatic retry with exponential backoff
- Resource isolation from real-time services
- Cost optimization (82% reduction with Spot)

**Implementation Complexity:** Low-Medium - Kubernetes Jobs/CronJobs are straightforward; complexity in parallelism and checkpointing

**Prerequisites:** Kubernetes cluster, batch namespace with ResourceQuota, idempotent processing logic, monitoring/alerting

**Related Patterns:** Event-Driven Processing, ML Model Serving, Resource Management, Unified Observability, CI/CD Pipeline
